documents.title: Estate distribution and receipt
documents.content:
Briarcombe Probate Services — beneficiary payment confirmation. Our reference EST-761204-AF. Client: Alice Fenwick. This file concerns the estate of her fictional aunt, Nora Fenwick. The executors authorised a final cash distribution of £325,000.00 to Alice on 14 August 2026. The enclosed estate account records the entitlement and the completion note records the transfer to Alice's nominated personal account. The payment reference was NF-ESTATE-FINAL. This is a completed inheritance receipt, rather than an estimate of a possible future legacy.

The estate account explains how the distributed money was assembled. Most of the cash came from the disposal of the deceased's long-held investment portfolio; the balance came from savings held in her sole name. Funeral costs, professional charges and the estate's liabilities were settled before the distributable residue was calculated. Alice's share was paid outright, with no continuing trust and no obligation to repay the money. The executor confirmation and the receipt refer to the same beneficiary and amount.

For the adviser, the immediate source of the proposed investment is the inherited cash now held by Alice. The underlying explanation for this addition to her wealth is the legacy from Nora's estate. The supporting papers establish the relationship between the estate entitlement, the authorised payment and the money received. They do not make claims about Alice's employment income, regular retirement income or overall investment performance. The adviser should retain the estate account alongside this signed confirmation when recording the funding rationale.

Alice has earmarked £200,000.00 of the receipt for a future investment proposal and wishes to keep the remainder readily available while she decides on home improvements. The allocation is an intention only and is not an instruction to trade. There is no request here to change her registered residential address. The beneficiary's contact address has intentionally been omitted from this extract because it is recorded separately in the client file. The confirmation is evidence of an actual inherited sum, not merely a will naming Alice as a prospective beneficiary, and it should not be confused with correspondence from another client asking about an inheritance that has not occurred.

documents.title: Completion bundle — tooling disposal
documents.content:
Sale completion record for Ravi Calderwick. Transaction reference BIZ-CW-260918. On 18 September 2026, Ravi completed the sale of his entire shareholding in Calderwick Precision Tools Ltd to Wrenhollow Manufacturing Holdings Ltd. Cash consideration was £2,400,000.00 before professional fees and the separately retained tax reserve. The signed completion statement and solicitor's receipt confirm that the consideration was paid, rather than being conditional on a future sale. There is no deferred earn-out in this transaction.

Ravi founded the business in 2004 and developed it from a small workshop into a supplier of specialist tooling. His ownership interest arose from his original subscription for shares and later retained business profits; it was not acquired through an unexplained recent transfer. The accompanying ownership schedule traces his holding from incorporation to completion. Those records explain how the business interest accumulated over time and why Ravi was entitled to receive the sale proceeds. The purchase agreement identifies the buyer and the shares transferred.

The net settlement was sent to Ravi's personal account after the solicitors deducted the agreed legal fees. He intends to invest £1,500,000.00 after retaining sufficient cash for known liabilities and ordinary household spending. The adviser has not treated the gross sale price as the sum available for immediate investment. The final tax liability remains a separate calculation, and this completion record does not certify any relief or tax treatment. It simply evidences the transaction and the receipt of consideration.

For source of funds review, the completed sale links the proposed investment to a specific, documented payment. For source of wealth review, the history of founding, owning and operating the business explains the origin of the asset sold. Both aspects are relevant to the client file. A generic brochure about selling a company would not establish either point for Ravi. His former employment by an energy supplier is part of his career history but is not the source of this receipt. No residential address is certified by the transaction papers. The bundle contains no pension transfer authority and makes no recommendation about an investment product; those matters require their own records and decisions.

documents.title: Completion statement — Orchard Row
documents.content:
Alderwick Conveyancing LLP. Client Alistair Fenwick. Property sale reference PROP-629104. Completion date 30 July 2026. The property sold was 19 Orchard Row, Merewick, a rental house that Alistair had acquired in 2012. The agreed sale price was £465,000.00. The completion statement records mortgage redemption of £112,000.00 and combined conveyancing and selling costs of £8,500.00, leaving net proceeds of £344,500.00. The solicitor confirms that this amount was remitted to Alistair on completion.

The supporting purchase history records that Alistair bought the house with accumulated illustration earnings and a mortgage. During his ownership he let it to tenants and met the mortgage payments from rental receipts and his own savings. This background explains the origin and development of the property asset; it is not a valuation of his current home. The sale contract, redemption statement and final ledger together show the route from ownership of the house to the cash now available to him. There is no outstanding condition requiring the buyer to make a further payment.

The adviser is retaining this bundle as evidence of the source of funds for a proposed investment and as supporting information about how this part of Alistair's wealth arose. Alistair plans to retain a cash reserve until his accountant has confirmed the tax position. The sale proceeds are a capital receipt, not his current salary or recurring trading income. The figures should therefore not be entered as monthly earnings in an affordability calculation. No tax conclusion is expressed in this document.

Orchard Row was an investment property and was not Alistair's residence at completion. His present home is recorded elsewhere in the client file, and these papers must not be used as proof of his current residential address simply because a street address appears in the text. The document also does not concern an inheritance, a gift or the sale of a company. The payment has already occurred, so it is materially different from an estate agent's estimate or a conversation about a possible future disposal. The original completion ledger has been checked against the solicitor's signed confirmation and filed with the client record.

documents.title: Executed testamentary instrument
documents.content:
Last will and testament of May Bellamy, signed on 22 September 2026 in the presence of two witnesses. This executed copy revokes May's earlier wills and appoints her brother, Owen Bellamy, and professional executor Cora Denswick to administer her estate. The original is held by Briarcombe Private Client Solicitors under reference WILL-MB-260922. The adviser has retained a copy to understand the client's estate planning intentions; no adviser is appointed as executor by this document.

The instrument leaves May's studio tools and finished ceramic works to her niece, Ada Bellamy. The residue of the estate is to be divided equally between Owen and Ada after liabilities and administration expenses have been paid. If either beneficiary dies before May, the substitution provisions in the signed instrument determine the destination of that share. A separate schedule describes the studio items so that the executor can identify them, but it does not provide a current market valuation. The will contains no direction to make an investment during May's lifetime.

May has discussed the document with her solicitor and understands that a will concerns the administration of her estate after death. It does not authorise another person to operate her bank accounts while she is alive and does not grant an attorney authority to manage her financial affairs. Those questions are addressed, where applicable, by a separate lasting power of attorney. The file note expressly distinguishes the roles of executor and attorney to avoid the documents being treated as interchangeable during a review meeting.

For the present client record, this is an executed estate planning document, not a draft, a blank template or evidence that a beneficiary has already received an inheritance. May remains alive and there has been no distribution from her estate. Names in the beneficiary clauses should not be mistaken for additional clients in this corpus. The adviser should refer any proposed change to the appointed solicitor and obtain an updated signed copy if the arrangements are changed. The file contains no assessment of inheritance tax due and no assurance that the instructions produce a particular tax outcome. Its relevance is the client's documented succession plan and the identification of her intended executors and beneficiaries.

documents.title: Settlement executed 2 October
documents.content:
Trust deed establishing the Calderwick Family Discretionary Trust on 2 October 2026. Settlor: Ravi Calderwick. Initial trustees: Ravi Calderwick and Cora Denswick. Deed reference TR-CAL-2602. The initial settled amount is £10.00. The named class of potential beneficiaries comprises Ravi's children and remoter descendants, together with the additional persons specified in the signed schedule. This is an executed settlement instrument, not a product brochure or a proposal awaiting signature.

The trustees hold the settled property under the terms of the deed and may consider appointments of income or capital within the powers and restrictions recorded in it. No individual beneficiary is recorded as entitled to a fixed payment on a fixed date. The administrative provisions address trustee appointments, record keeping and the exercise of discretion. The adviser has retained the document to understand the structure when discussing Ravi's wider estate planning arrangements; the extract is not intended to replace reading the complete signed deed.

A separately signed letter of wishes gives Ravi's personal guidance about education expenditure. That letter is distinct from this instrument and does not override the trustees' duties or the terms of the settlement. The two documents should be reviewed together when an adviser needs context, but a search for the binding trust deed should not treat the non-binding letter as the deed itself. Neither document is Ravi's will, and neither grants an attorney power to manage his personal accounts during his lifetime.

Only the nominal initial settlement is evidenced here. There has been no subsequent transfer of the proceeds of Ravi's business sale into the trust under this deed as filed. The document therefore does not establish the source of funds for a large subscription, does not show the value of Ravi's personal estate and does not confirm any investment holding. If further assets are settled, separate evidence of the transfer and its origin will be required. No conclusion about tax efficiency, residence or beneficial entitlement should be inferred beyond the signed provisions. The purpose of retaining this copy is to record the existing legal arrangement and the identities of the settlor and trustees, not to present a future funding intention as a completed transaction.

documents.title: Household review workbook
documents.content:
Fact find completed with Alice Fenwick on 8 October 2026. Household planning label: Project Copperfin. Alice recently retired from engineering management and wants to organise her cash before committing to a long-term investment. She has no financial dependants and expects to meet routine spending from existing resources while she reviews when to draw retirement benefits. The information below records her statements during the meeting; figures have not all been independently verified by this workbook.

Alice estimates essential household spending at £2,100.00 a month and discretionary spending at £650.00 a month. She wishes to retain an accessible emergency reserve of £30,000.00 and has provisionally set aside £45,000.00 for home improvements. She has no unsecured borrowing. She regards capital needed within the next two years as unavailable for long-term market investment. The adviser recorded these constraints before discussing products so that the eventual recommendation can be tested against her practical needs.

Her main objective is to preserve spending flexibility while allowing part of her capital to grow over at least ten years. She has previously held collective investments but has not traded derivatives or borrowed to invest. She says that an extended fall in markets would make her uncomfortable if it affected money needed for household bills. The separate risk questionnaire explores her attitude to volatility and the adviser will discuss capacity for loss independently. The fact find itself is not a completed risk score or a suitability recommendation.

Alice also reported a recent family estate distribution, for which the signed receipt is held separately. This workbook does not independently establish the origin of that money, and it should not replace the supporting estate papers in an evidence search. No certified identity copy, residential bill or tax residence declaration forms part of this document. The review records client circumstances and objectives so that later advice can be tailored and explained. Alice agreed to check the expenditure figures and report any material omissions before the recommendation is finalised. There is no instruction to invest, transfer a pension or take out insurance at this stage, and no recommendation should be inferred from the list of products mentioned during the conversation.

documents.title: Investor questionnaire — completed
documents.content: Alice Fenwick completed the investment risk questionnaire on 8 October 2026. Score 42/80, indicative profile balanced. She would tolerate temporary market falls in long-term capital but needs certainty for near-term spending. Adviser note: attitude to risk and capacity for loss were discussed separately; the score alone is not a recommendation. Signed responses are retained, not a blank questionnaire.

documents.title: Personal recommendation — October
documents.content:
Suitability report for Alice Fenwick, dated 16 October 2026. Household planning label: Project Copperfin. This report explains the recommendation arising from the completed fact find, the discussion of investment risk and the review of accessible reserves. Alice's objective is to invest £200,000.00 for a period of at least ten years while keeping separate cash for planned works and unforeseen expenditure. The recommendation is based on the circumstances recorded at the review and should be revisited if those circumstances change.

The proposed approach is a diversified portfolio of collective funds aligned with the agreed balanced risk profile. The adviser considered Alice's experience, her reaction to previous market falls and her ability to meet spending without selling investments at an unfavourable time. Capacity for loss was assessed separately from her willingness to accept volatility. A portfolio suitable for long-term growth may fall in value and is unsuitable for cash needed to meet near-term household commitments. The proposed accessible reserve is therefore excluded from the investment allocation.

Alternatives considered included leaving all the money in cash and adopting a lower-risk investment mix. Cash would preserve nominal accessibility but would not meet the same long-term growth objective; the lower-risk mix would alter the balance between expected variability and growth potential. These comparisons explain the personalised recommendation rather than promising a return. Charges and service arrangements are set out in the accompanying disclosure, and Alice is to receive the relevant product information before deciding whether to proceed. This report does not confirm that any trade has taken place.

The file records that supporting evidence for the origin of the investment money has been reviewed separately. This report is not itself a bank receipt, estate account or certified identity document. It contains no pension transfer recommendation and no recommendation to buy life assurance. Its role is to connect Alice's needs, resources, time horizon and risk discussion to the proposed investment approach. Alice should read the report and raise any factual correction before authorising implementation. A later change in spending plans, available capital or ability to withstand loss may require a new assessment; the report is specific to the facts recorded for this review.

queries.why: Current residential evidence is required, the licence and historical bill are reasonable secondary hits for this unqualified query, and requests or delivery receipts do not establish residence.

queries.q: document confirming where the client currently lives
queries.why: The current residential records directly answer the request, while the current licence and self-reported change of address offer additional context rather than the independently accepted evidence.

Electricity, gas, water and fixed-line broadband bills are household utility bills, including the archived bill because no recency constraint is given, whereas requests for a missing bill are not bills.

queries.q: current proof of address for Imogen Harrowby
queries.why: The signed tenancy is accepted current evidence for Imogen, while her old electricity account is explicitly superseded and other clients’ residential evidence is irrelevant.
The broadband bill supplies the requested evidence despite its generic title, whereas the earlier e-mail only requests a bill and the courier receipt does not prove residence.
The Hearthmere account records actual domestic gas charges even though its title does not name the document type.
The Mossmere document bills the client for water and sewerage services.
The local authority demand is an issued council tax bill, unlike a self-assessment tax calculation.
The current account statement is the actual bank record, whereas an e-mail asking for a bank statement supplies no statement.
The signed occupancy agreement contains the residential tenancy terms and both parties’ signatures.
The home loan summary is the current mortgage statement, while the property sale completion ledger merely records a mortgage redemption.
The passport, photocard driving licence and national identity card each provide verified photographic identity evidence; a passport holder and a passport metaphor do not.

queries.q: Imogen Harrowby e-mail about a possible future inheritance
queries.why: The speculative legacy enquiry is the requested correspondence even though it cannot prove received funds, and Alice’s completed inheritance belongs to a different client.
The certified travel document is an actual passport copy, while the wallet receipt, marketing metaphor and evidence-request e-mail are not passports.
The photocard copy records an actual driving licence and its verification.
The identity check contains the verified national identity card rather than a passport or residency declaration.
Issued payroll, annual earnings, tax computation and accountant confirmation establish income, while capital receipts, uncompleted forms and pension valuations do not evidence recurring earnings.

queries.q: documents confirming how much the client earns
queries.why: These four records establish actual employment or self-employed income, unlike a capital sale, account balance or blank earnings template.
The September payroll advice is an issued monthly payslip, distinct from the annual P60.
The issued annual certificate is the primary client document, although the explicitly labelled blank P60 is a reasonable secondary hit for an unqualified type search.
Only Maya’s completed employer certificate satisfies the request; the blank training form belongs to May and merely mentions Maya in a warning.
The filed tax computation records self-assessment income and is not a tax residency certificate.
The signed professional confirmation is expressly an accountant’s letter establishing Imogen’s completed trading profit.
Completed inheritance, business sale and property sale records trace actual capital receipts, whereas intentions, recommendations and generic marketing do not establish the origin of funds.
The estate record identifies inherited wealth and both sale bundles explain how the underlying assets arose, while balances and a nominal trust settlement alone do not explain accumulated wealth.

queries.q: paperwork showing money actually received from an inheritance
queries.why: The estate distribution confirms an actual beneficiary payment, unlike a living client’s will or an enquiry about a possible future legacy.
The completion bundle evidences Ravi’s completed disposal and receipt, while the newsletter’s identical headline amount is hypothetical.
The Orchard Row completion ledger records the realised property sale proceeds, not the outstanding balance on a current home loan.
The self-certification declares tax residence, while tax computations and nationality on an identity card do not establish tax residency.
The signed declaration explicitly covers both CRS tax residence and FATCA status.
The executed testamentary instrument is the client’s will, whereas a possible legacy enquiry and documents distinguishing themselves from a will are not wills.
The registered financial authority is an LPA, while the will’s explanation of attorney roles is not an LPA instrument.
The private guidance is the actual signed letter; the trust deed merely refers to the separately held letter.
The executed settlement establishes the trust, whereas the non-binding letter of wishes cannot substitute for the deed.
The will, financial LPA, wishes and trust deed document clients’ succession or lifetime planning, unlike probate evidence about a deceased relative or speculative correspondence.
